baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the symbol definitions and the Region 3 torque-speed relationship faithfully with supporting quotes. Set B additionally includes the definition of IGen (generator inertia relative to the high-speed shaft), which is a real definition on the page that Set A omits. Otherwise the two sets are identical, including the same redundancy where θ is stated twice (as a definition and as a symbol claim).
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets state the θ blade-pitch angle fact twice (definition claim and symbol claim), a mild duplication pattern. Neither set extracts the PID gain definitions (KP, KI, KD) or the rated speed Ω0 definition, which are notable facts on the page. The text layer is largely clean; the equation fragments are garbled but the surrounding prose is readable.

variant-first.note: Both sets are faithful and accurate on the shared claims, with quotes that match the page and correct Region 3 conditions on the generator-torque relationship. Set A additionally captures the definition of IGen (generator inertia relative to the high-speed shaft), which Set B omits, so A covers the symbol list more completely. Neither set misreads or invents anything; both repeat the θ/blade-pitch-angle fact under two names. Because the only difference is one correct claim present in A and missing in B, A is slightly better.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets state the θ definition twice (as 'θ | definition' and as 'blade-pitch angle | symbol | θ'), a harmless duplication. Both also leave out other symbol definitions on the page (Ω0 rated low-speed shaft speed, Ω low-speed shaft rotational speed, t simulation time, and the KP/KI/KD PID gains), so the omission is symmetric except for IGen.

variant-first.note: Both sets share the same five chordwise-center claims from Figure 2-11, so the difference is Set A's two axial-stiffness claims. Set A reads the y-axis tick '0' as a value at r/R = 0.0 and the axis multiplier '1e10' as a value at r/R = 1.0; the plotted curve actually starts near 4.5e10 N at the root and ends near 0.2e10 N at the tip. Set B omits axial stiffness entirely but adds nothing wrong, so it is the more faithful set.
variant-first.remarks: Set A's two axial-stiffness claims are axis-label artifacts: '0' is a y-axis tick and '1e10' is the scale multiplier, not data points; the quotes are assembled from axis text and do not support the claimed values. Both sets leave out the mass-density, edgewise/flapwise/torsional stiffness and axial-stiffness curves of Figure 2-10 (only curve values are readable, so exact numbers would need chart reading). The five 'structural property center' claims are legend labels of Figure 2-11 with a vague shared attribute; they would be better stated as chordwise offsets of the pitch axis / mass / neutral / geometric / shear centers versus blade span.

baseline-first.note: Both sets give the same five Figure 2-11 legend entries (pitch axis, mass/neutral/geometric/shear center), which are correct but essentially label-level claims. Set B adds two axial-stiffness claims that are wrong: it reads the axis tick labels as data, asserting 0 N at r/R = 0.0 and 1e10 N at r/R = 1.0, whereas plot (c) shows roughly 4.5e10 N at the root and near zero at the tip (1e10 is the axis multiplier). Set A therefore has no wrong claims while Set B has two misread/misbound ones, so A is better despite both omitting the mass-density and edge/flap/torsional stiffness data.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets miss the substantive content of Figure 2-10: mass density vs span, and edge/flap/torsional stiffness vs span. The five 'structural property center' claims are just legend labels of Figure 2-11 with no values or span positions, so they carry little engineering content. Set B's axial-stiffness claims appear to be generated by pairing axis tick labels (0, 1e10) with x-axis endpoints rather than reading the curve.

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content; the only differences are in the Young's modulus and shear modulus of steel claims, where A binds the values to 'tower steel' and keeps the Table 4-1 condition while B uses the vaguer entity 'steel' and drops the condition. Both sets share the same weaknesses: three overlapping claims about the tower's first natural frequency (0.18 Hz, 0.17 Hz, 0.170 Hz), one of which (0.18 Hz) contradicts the stated 0.170 Hz. A is marginally more precise and faithful, so it is the better set.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets report the tower 1st natural frequency three times (0.18 Hz, 0.17 Hz, 0.170 Hz); the 0.18 Hz value contradicts the text's 0.170 Hz and appears to be a misread of the figure line. The 1P (0.09-0.13 Hz) and 3P (0.25-0.38 Hz) ranges and the wave-spectrum peak at 0.11 Hz are read off Figure 4-1 and are approximate but plausible. Important facts both sets omit: the 7% outfitting mass allowance, the 100 t transition piece mass, the requirement for a stiffer tower with a floating/semisubmersible substructure, and the soil being modeled with spring constants representative of dense sand or gravel.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical, sharing 16 claims including the same table values, geometry facts, and figure readings. The only differences are the Young's modulus and shear modulus claims: Set B binds them to 'tower steel' and keeps the Table 4-1 source condition, while Set A gives the vaguer entity 'steel' and drops the condition. Both sets contain the same misread (tower 1st natural frequency 0.18 Hz, contradicting the stated 0.170 Hz) and duplicate that fact under two names/values.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets report the tower 1st natural frequency twice with inconsistent values (0.18 Hz and 0.17 Hz); the text layer clearly states 0.170 Hz, so 0.18 Hz is a misread and the pair is a duplicate. The 1P (0.09-0.13 Hz) and 3P (0.25-0.38 Hz) ranges and the wave/wind PSD readings are taken from Figure 4-1 and are only approximately verifiable from the plot. Both sets omit the 7% outfitting mass allowance, the 100 t transition piece mass, and the note that a floating substructure requires a stiffer tower.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are essentially identical in content: same nine facts plus the same tenth, differing only in capitalization and singular/plural of 'handrail(s)'. Both bind 2' - 9 1/2" to the Evacuated Solar Thermal Tubes as a height, but on the page that dimension is the FINISHED FLOOR elevation marker; the quoted string is a fabricated concatenation of two separate labels. Both also state the 1/8" cable railing dimension twice (as thickness and diameter), and both omit the finished-floor elevation as its own claim.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets make the same misbinding: 2' - 9 1/2" is the FINISHED FLOOR level marker (with GRADE LEVEL 0' - 0" and SOLAR ENVELOPE 18' - 0" as the other datum markers), not a height of the solar thermal tubes. The quote 'EVACUATED SOLAR THERMAL TUBES 2' - 9 1/2"' does not appear on the page and stitches two unrelated labels together. The 1/8" steel cable railing is stated twice under two attribute names (thickness and diameter) in both sets. Both sets also leave out the finished floor elevation as a correctly bound claim and the note that tube array spacing may be larger with valves/piping not shown.

variant-first.note: The two sets contain the same ten claims with only trivial naming differences ("handrail" vs "handrails", capitalization of the tube entity), so their engineering content is identical. Both bind the 2' - 9 1/2" dimension to the Evacuated Solar Thermal Tubes, when the text layer shows that value belongs to FINISHED FLOOR; both also state the 1/8" cable railing dimension twice (thickness and diameter). Neither set captures the finished floor elevation as its own claim, and both treat the 18' - 0" solar envelope marker as a height rather than an elevation.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets splice separate text-layer lines into the quote "EVACUATED SOLAR THERMAL TUBES 2' - 9 1/2"", which misreads the drawing: 2' - 9 1/2" is the FINISHED FLOOR level marker, not a tube dimension. The finished floor elevation is therefore effectively lost in both sets. The 1/8" steel cable railing is one fact stated under two attribute names (thickness and diameter) in both sets. The 18' - 0" SOLAR ENVELOPE value is an elevation/level marker like GRADE LEVEL 0' - 0", so calling it "height" is questionable in both sets.

baseline-first.note: The two sets contain the same three claims with the same values and quotes; the only difference is how the 'S-301' reference next to the through-bolt callout is handled. Set A keeps it inside the quote, which is harmless, while Set B promotes it to a 'condition', misbinding a sheet/detail reference as an engineering condition. Otherwise both bind the 3/8" bolt diameter and the L3X3X1/4 angle designation correctly, and both carry the same questionable 'C1 thickness 3/16"' claim.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets assert 'C1 | thickness | 3/16"' but 3/16" does not appear in the text layer and C1 is a detail callout (MODULE B - PV STRUCTURAL MEMBER - NORTH/SOUTH), not a component with a stated thickness; this claim looks misbound or unsupported in both. The L3X3X1/4 claim states the designation as a 'dimension' with unit '"', which is redundant/odd since the value already encodes the units. Many dimension strings in the text layer (e.g. 10'-3 3/4", 12'-3 3/4", 2'-2 7/8") and the 3/8" THROUGH BOLT quantity/location are not claimed by either sample, but since the samples are declared complete for both, this is neutral.

variant-first.note: Both sets contain the same three claims in a different order, so they are substantively identical. Both correctly capture the 3/8" through bolt diameter (with the S-301 reference kept), but both also assert 'C1 | thickness | 3/16"', where C1 is a detail callout bubble and 3/16" only appears inside the dimension '6 3/16"' — a misbound/unsupported claim whose quote is not on the page. Both repeat the angle designation L3X3X1/4 as a 'dimension', which is a tautological, trivial claim with a misapplied unit.
variant-first.remarks: The two sets are the same claims reordered; the only difference is that A puts the S-301 reference in 'conditions' while B appends it to the quote — both are acceptable renderings. The quote 'C1 3/16"' does not occur in the text layer (the layer has 'C1' and '6 3/16"' as separate strings), so it cannot support a thickness claim. Both sets omit the substantive geometry on the page (e.g. 12'-3 3/4", 10'-3 3/4", 7'-0", 3'-8 3/8" member/dimension strings and the L3X3X1/4 angle callouts as member designations). Note the text layer is a spatially scrambled token dump, so quote fidelity should be judged against the image as well.

variant-first.note: Set A covers far more of the page correctly (equipment, wall base, accent paint, VCT and millwork rows), while Set B is clean but sparse, omitting many facts A captures. However, A mixes up the Finish/Floor-Finish and Plumbing schedules, binding VINYL COMPOSITE TILE attributes to SHOWER VALVE and vice versa (style name STANDARD EXCELON, style number 51899, model T17059), with quotes that do not support those claims. B has no misbound or invented claims but leaves out a lot of the schedule content. On balance A's breadth of correct claims outweighs its four misbindings, though it is not clean.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets state four millwork rows (MWK04, MWK05, MWB02, MWB03) twice, differing only in the condition label ('Tag ...' vs 'Millwork Schedule') — a duplication pattern worth suppressing. The text layer reorders rows within the Furniture and Millwork schedules, so tag-to-row binding must be checked against the image; here the millwork bindings in both sets match the image. A's 'VINYL COMPOSITE TILE | texture | IMPERIAL TEXTURE' also invents an attribute: the page lists IMPERIAL TEXTURE as part of the style name 'STANDARD EXCELON IMPERIAL TEXTURE'.

variant-first.note: Both sets are largely accurate and share 21 identical claims, but Set B binds the wall-base claim to tag WB and preserves the MDF material from the profile field, which Set A truncates to "4\" H x 1/2\" THK". Set B also binds the accent-paint colour to P3 (Accent Paint) explicitly, whereas Set A leaves it as the bare description "ACCENT PAINT". Both sets invent a "KITCHEN" location for the quartz and restate the glass location as "BATHROOM SHOWER" (the sheet says SHOWER SURROUND), and both omit the same facts (tile style/colour numbers, Fireclay Tile as GT manufacturer, P3 colour number 33-14, several millwork rows and quantities).
variant-first.remarks: The QZ (quartz) block on the sheet has no LOCATION field at all, so the "location: KITCHEN" condition in both sets is unsupported; the GL location reads "SHOWER SURROUND", not "BATHROOM SHOWER". Both sets also leave out notable finish-schedule data (PT1/PT2 style numbers FGEEOB412/FGEEOB1224, colour OBSIDIAN BLACK, GT manufacturer FIRECLAY TILE / style CRUSH / colour DANDELION, P3 colour number 33-14 and finishes, WB finish and location) and millwork rows MWK01, MWK03, MWK04, MWB01, MWL01, MWD02 with their quantities. The text layer scrambles the millwork table row/column order, so row-to-dimension binding must be checked against the image; both sets did this correctly for the rows they used.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are nearly identical and largely faithful to the Finish and Millwork schedules, but Set A keeps the wall base material (MDF) as a condition and tags the accent paint claim with P3, while Set B drops MDF from the wall base profile claim and states the accent paint only by description. Both sets add an unsupported 'location: KITCHEN' condition to the quartz claims and render the glass location 'SHOWER SURROUND' as 'BATHROOM SHOWER'. Set B's omission of the MDF material is the only real loss of engineering information, so A is marginally better.
baseline-first.remarks: The page never states a KITCHEN location for the quartz (QZ) entry, which has no LOCATION field at all; both sets invented that condition (2 claims each). The glass (GL) location is printed as 'SHOWER SURROUND', not 'BATHROOM SHOWER' — a mild paraphrase both sets share. Also, the quantity claims quote only the bare numeral '2', which does not by itself support binding to MWB02/MWB03; the text layer is heavily jumbled (tags and values out of row order), so row binding should be checked against the image, which is legible.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the controller goals, operating ranges, filter type and variable definitions accurately, but Set A additionally includes the important fact that generator speed measurement is the sole feedback input for both controllers and that nacelle-yaw regulation was not developed. Set B omits both of these and instead adds a near-trivial claim that the baseline control system uses a conventional design approach. Set A's weakness is redundancy: the feedback-input fact is stated four times (per controller, with two different condition fields) and the filter-type fact twice. Set B repeats the nonpower-production claim under two entity names while missing the feedback-input and nacelle-yaw facts.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets duplicate the filter-type claim (recursive single-pole low-pass with exponential smoothing) under two condition variants; this is a shared pattern rather than a differentiator. The filter equations (7-1), (7-2), (7-3a) and the definitions of alpha, n, Ts and fc are not claimed by either set.

baseline-first.note: Set B captures two important facts that A omits: that both controllers use the generator speed measurement as the sole feedback input, and that no control actions were developed to regulate the nacelle-yaw angle. Set A instead repeats the nonpower-production claim under two different entity names and adds a near-trivial 'conventional design approach' claim. Both sets bind the two-control-system and filter-type claims correctly and share the same mild over-attribution of the generic 'such wind turbines' control architecture to the NREL 5-MW turbine. B is somewhat more repetitive (three duplicated fact pairs vs. A's two), but its coverage of substantive facts is clearly better.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets state the filter-type fact twice with only differing condition wording, and B additionally splits the sole-feedback-input fact into four claims (per controller x per condition). Neither set extracts the filter equations (7-1), (7-2), (7-3a) or the definitions of alpha, n, Ts, fc, which are the main quantitative content of Section 7.1.

variant-first.note: Both sets are accurate on the claims they share (torque saturation 47,402.91 N•m, 15,000 N•m/s rate limit, rated generator speed 1173.7 rpm, high drivetrain damping, no torsional-vibration control loop). Set A additionally captures the key controller architecture facts: gain-scheduled PI control on speed error in Region 3, and the conditional that torque is computed as in Region 3 whenever the previous blade-pitch command is 1º or greater. Set B instead adds two correct but less central modeling details (single-DOF = shaft angular rotation, control goal = regulate generator speed) and omits the conditional logic and PI control method. No claim in either set is wrong, so A wins on coverage of important facts.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets miss the stated trade-off of the conditional logic (improved output power quality at the expense of short-term generator/gearbox overloading) and the 10%-above-rated basis of the 47,402.91 N•m saturation, though the saturation quote itself conveys the 10% figure.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are accurate on the five shared claims (rated speed 1173.7 rpm, 47,402.91 N·m saturation, 15,000 N·m/s rate limit, high drivetrain damping, no torsional-vibration loop), with faithful quotes and correct bindings. Set B additionally captures the important conditional torque logic (Region-3 computation when the previous blade-pitch command is 1° or greater) and the gain-scheduled PI control method with its Region 3 condition, both well supported. Set A instead adds the single-DOF model's degree of freedom and the control goal, which are correct but less central, and it omits the conditional statement entirely. B therefore covers more of the key engineering content without introducing errors.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets omit the stated rationale/trade-off (improved output power quality at the expense of short-term generator and gearbox overloading) and the fact that the blade-pitch system takes over in Region 3; these are secondary but useful context. Set B's 'control input' attribute is slightly generic but the value and quote are correct.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in values, bindings and quotes; the only difference is that Set B adds the condition 'S-301' to the 3/8" through bolt claim, which is supported since both through-bolt callouts sit in details keyed to S-301 (C1 S-301 and A4 S-301). Both sets read the dimension values correctly and keep left/right and top/bottom segment conditions where used. Both also share the same weaknesses: vague entities ('right-side component', 'dimension', truncated 'MEMBER - NORTH/SOUTH'), repeated facts (7'-0" and 12'-3 3/4" each stated twice, 1 1/2" left side given under two entity names), and many page dimensions left unextracted. Set B's added, correct condition gives it a slight edge.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets bind many dimensions to placeholder entities ('right-side component', 'dimension') rather than to the actual members/details shown (MODULE A and MODULE B PV structural members, details C1 S-301 and A4 S-301, L3X3X1/4 angles, 3/8" through bolts). Numerous dimensions on the page (3'-8 3/8", 3'-1 5/16", 2'-2 7/8", 6 3/16", 1'-8 11/16", 2'-3 7/8", 6 13/16", 1'-11 1/8", 2'-5 5/16", 4 3/4", 3", 2", 6") are extracted by neither set. The text layer garbles the detail titles as 'DULE B/A - PV STRUCTURAL MEMBER - NORTH/SOUTH' (MODULE truncated), which likely caused the truncated entity name in both sets.

variant-first.note: The two sets are identical except for a single claim: Set A adds the condition "S-301" to the 3/8" through-bolt claim, which is supported by the C1 S-301 and A4 S-301 detail callouts shown on the page, so it is not an error but also not a decisive improvement. Both sets read the dimension strings correctly (10'-3 3/4", 12'-3 3/4", 7'-0", 3'-6", 7 1/16", 4 13/16", 1 1/2", 5/8", 3/8" THROUGH BOLT, L3X3X1/4) and both bind them to vague placeholder entities such as "right-side component", "C1 S-301 component" and "dimension". Both also repeat 7'-0" and 12'-3 3/4" under two names and include a garbled entity "MEMBER - NORTH/SOUTH". With the same strengths and the same weaknesses, the sets are effectively equivalent.
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions use generic placeholder entities ("right-side component", "C1 S-301 component", "dimension", "structural member") instead of naming the actual members (angles L3X3X1/4, PV structural member, base/plate details), so most claims are only weakly bound even though the quoted values are read correctly. The entity "MEMBER - NORTH/SOUTH" is a truncation of the garbled text-layer title "DULE A/B - PV STRUCTURAL MEMBER - NORTH/SOUTH". 7'-0" and 12'-3 3/4" are each stated twice (once under a module title, once as a bare "dimension"), and several bare dimension claims (3"-8 3/8", 3'-1 5/16", 2'-2 7/8", 6 3/16", 1'-8 11/16", 2'-5 5/16", 1'-11 1/8", 4 3/4", 6 13/16", 2'-3 7/8") present on the page are not claimed by either set. The text layer is badly fragmented (title lines cut to "DULE B/A"), so entity naming relies on the image.

variant-first.note: The two sets are essentially identical in content: the same 22 claims, differing only in wording ('science instrument count' vs 'instrument count', 'Lynx' vs 'Lynx mirror assembly' for the 10 m focal length). Both capture the correct baseline specs (HabEx 4 m/4 instruments/52 m starshade, LUVOIR-A 15 m/4, LUVOIR-B 8 m/3, Lynx 3 m/10 m focal length/3, Origins 5.9 m/3) and both make the same errors. Neither is better on correctness, coverage, or faithfulness.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets share identical defects: fragment entities 'n-axis telescope' and 'axis telescope' (text-layer artifacts of 'on-axis'/'off-axis') with instrument counts misbound away from LUVOIR-A/LUVOIR-B; 'grazing incidence mirror assembly' given the 3 science instruments (belongs to Lynx as a mission) and given 10 m as 'dimension'/'diameter' when 10 m is the focal length; vague 'spacecraft | science instrument count | 4' (actually the HabEx telescope spacecraft); duplicate starshade-diameter and Lynx 3 m claims. Several quotes are truncated or garbled ('grazing incidence mir', 'a 10 m nd three science instruments', 'Lynx: ... and three science instruments'). All substantive facts on the page are covered by both sets.

baseline-first.note: The two sets contain essentially the same 22 claims, differing only in ordering and trivial entity naming (e.g., A's 'Lynx mirror assembly | focal length | 10 m' vs B's 'Lynx | focal length | 10 m', and 'instrument count' vs 'science instrument count'). Both correctly capture the baseline telescope/mirror diameters, focal length, instrument counts and the 52 m starshade. Both share the same defects: truncated entities ('n-axis telescope', 'axis telescope'), the 10 m focal length misbound as a mirror-assembly dimension/diameter, the Lynx instrument count misbound to the mirror assembly, a vague 'spacecraft' entity, and duplicated starshade claims.
baseline-first.remarks: Shared defects in both sets: 'n-axis telescope' and 'axis telescope' are truncated fragments of 'on-axis'/'off-axis telescope' (misread entities); 'grazing incidence mirror assembly | dimension/diameter | 10 m' misreads the 10 m focal length as a size (the assembly diameter is 3 m); 'grazing incidence mirror assembly | science instrument count | 3' misbinds the Lynx instrument count to the mirror assembly; 'spacecraft | science instrument count | 4' and the bare 'on-axis/off-axis telescope' entities are vague; the 52 m starshade claim appears twice in each set. Both sets also drop the 'flying in formation' condition on the starshade and the fact that it is a separate spacecraft.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical; A adds a supported through-bolt length of 4" while B adds a plywood thickness claim (supported) and a through-bolt diameter claim carrying the condition 'S-301', which appears nowhere on this sheet (the sheet is S-522). Both sets share the same questionable bindings (1" attributed to a 'nut sleeve' when the label is a 1" NUT with SLEVE as a separate item; 4 1/4" attributed to landscape footing width when it dimensions the rod/sleeve assembly in detail A6) and both repeat the 2"x8" and 3/4"x5 1/2" facts under two names. Because B introduces an invented condition and A introduces nothing unsupported, A is the better set.
baseline-first.remarks: Shared issues in both sets: 'nut sleeve | dimension | 1"' misreads the label '1" NUT / SLEVE' (1" is the nut size, sleeve is a separate part); 'landscape footing | component width | 4 1/4"' binds a dimension of the threaded-rod/sleeve assembly in detail A6 to the footing; 'decking footing plan | overall depth | 1'-0"' is a misbound/vague reading of a plan dimension. Both sets also state the 2"x8" joist/frame and 3/4"x5 1/2" surface facts twice under different entity names. Neither set captures the 3/4" threaded rod, 4X4 cut-as-needed, 8'-0" or the 1 1/2" / 7 1/2" section dimensions.

variant-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims, including several duplicated pairs (joist/deck joist, frame/deck frame, reclaimed wood surface twice) and a couple of misbound dimension strings. Set A adds two flawed claims: a through-bolt diameter claim carrying an invented 'S-301' condition not present anywhere on the page, and a 'deck | plywood thickness | 3/4"' claim that misbinds the plywood-deck cross-section to the deck as a thickness and duplicates an existing claim. Set B instead adds a correct and useful through-bolt length (4") claim, so B is the more faithful set.
variant-first.remarks: Shared issues in both sets: 'nut sleeve | dimension | 1"' merges two separate labels (1" NUT and SLEVE) and misbinds the nut size; 'decking footing plan | overall depth | 1'-0"' calls a plan dimension an overall depth; 'landscape footing | component width | 4 1/4"' has a vague attribute for a dimension that appears twice in detail A6. Both sets also omit notable page facts such as the 3/4" THREADED ROD, 1" NUT / SLEVE assembly in A6, 4X4 TO BE CUT AS NEEDED, and the 8'-0" and 7 1/2" dimensions. The text layer is a flat dump with no positional binding, so several dimension strings (1'-0", 4 1/4", 1 1/4", 3 3/4") cannot be reliably tied to a specific feature from text alone.

variant-first.note: The two sets are essentially identical in content: same 19 claims, same values, quotes and bindings, with only a trivial ordering difference and Set A adding the condition 'load of laundry' to the clothes-drying eligibility claim (which is really the subject, not a condition). Both correctly capture the dishwasher temperature thresholds (120°F full, 115°F half), sensor redundancy, capacity, heated-drying disablement, and the Figure 8 weight-based scoring bands. Both also repeat the same facts under two names (scoring bands under 'Clothes Dryer Subcontest' and 'clothes-drying task', sensor count, 120°F, 115°F, wash/rinse cycle) and both omit several substantive rules on the page.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets are near-duplicates of each other; the only delta is Set A's extra 'load of laundry' condition, which is immaterial. Both miss important page facts: the temperature-of-record rule (higher of two sensor readings, lower if the higher-reading sensor is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption', cycle completion confirmed by audible/visible signal, permitted load states (empty/partial/full, soiled/clean), the two-loads-per-day requirement with separately scored double loads, the requirement that visible drying methods be demonstrated to the architecture and market appeal juries, and the Contest 9-1 lighting requirement. 'Dishwasher | operation mode | automatic' is a trivial fragment duplicating the minimum-cycle-requirements claim.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are essentially identical: all 19 claims match in entity, attribute, value, unit and quote, with the sole difference that Set B adds the condition "load of laundry" to the clothes-drying eligibility claim. Both sets correctly bind the dishwasher temperatures (120 °F full points, 115 °F half points), the 8-place-setting capacity, the two-sensor redundancy, the disabled heated-drying option, and the Clothes Dryer Subcontest weight thresholds (≤100 / 100–110 / ≥110 % of original weight), with quotes that support them. Both sets also repeat the same facts under two names (sensor count, wash/rinse cycles, 120 °F, 115 °F, and the three scoring bands stated both under "Clothes Dryer Subcontest" and "clothes-drying task"), and both omit the same facts (temperature-of-record rule, cycle-completion signal, cycle-interruption definition, load state allowance, two-loads-per-day rule). The single added condition in B is too marginal to make the sets meaningfully different.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets double-state several facts (2 sensors, 1 wash/rinse cycle, 120 °F, 115 °F, and each of the three clothes-drying scoring bands under both "Clothes Dryer Subcontest" and "clothes-drying task"), inflating the count without adding information. Shared omissions worth adding: the higher-of-two-sensor-readings temperature-of-record rule (with the defective-sensor exception), cycle completion confirmed by audible/visible signal, the definition of cycle "interruption", the allowance to run the dishwasher empty/partially/fully loaded and soiled or clean, the two-loads-per-day requirement with separately scored loads, and the requirement to demonstrate towel-visible drying methods to the architecture and market appeal juries.

baseline-first.note: Set B reproduces all of Set A's claims and adds five correct wiring-schedule facts (150 conduit 2-1/2"C and #4G ground, 34 conductors 6#10 and 1"C conduit, item 33 #10G ground) that Set A omits, giving B materially better coverage of the schedule. B's one real defect is the claim 'Wiring 113 | 3#4/0 | AL, ARMORED CABLE' with quote '113 AL: 3#4/0, ARMORED CABLE': 113 is the lot number in the title block, the schedule item is 151, and that quote does not exist on the page. Both sets share the same error of reading '3W' as the phase of the sub-panel (the note reads 1~, 3W, i.e. single-phase, three-wire) and both state the 50A/2P main breaker twice under different entities. On balance B's five additional correct, substantive claims outweigh its single misread claim.
baseline-first.remarks: The text layer is badly jumbled: schedule symbol numbers are separated from their description rows (e.g. '50 AL: 3#4/0, #4G., 2-1/2"C.' is almost certainly the 150 row, and '150'/'20'/'31' float free of their lines), so row-to-description binding was judged mainly from the page image and from claims both sets agree on. B's chart claims appear to be generated by pairing axis tick labels with series names rather than reading the plotted curves; the '0.2 at 20º' gain-correction factor claim is the only one roughly consistent with the curve (~0.24) but its quote is still a spliced label string. baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical and share the same defective claims — truncated WC model strings (C454CUFG#0 / C454CUFG# instead of C454CUFG#01), shower-head model 52655 misbound to the location 'BATHROOM SHOWER', and SV/SH locations truncated to 'BATHROOM' — so those cancel out. Set A keeps the tag conditions needed to disambiguate the two BRIZO faucets (model BSP-L-65014LF-PC tagged F2, location KITCHEN tagged F1), which Set B drops. Set B's single advantage is binding the Delta manufacturer claim to SHOWER VALVE, where Set A uses the vague entity 'Shower' with a garbled quote. On balance A is slightly more faithful because it preserves two needed conditions against B's one better-named entity.
baseline-first.remarks: Text layer is badly garbled over the FINISH SCHEDULE block (fragments like 'QU', 'FIE', 'PR', 'DE', '33'), so finish-schedule claims cannot be verified from the text alone; the image is the only reliable source there. Both sets invent the labels 'option 1'/'option 2' for the two F10 PATIO SIDE TABLE (S/2) dimension rows — the page shows two rows of a set-of-two, not options. Both sets also carry the garbled quote 'DESCRIPTION: SHOWE MANUFACTURER: DELTA', which is not verbatim on the page (source reads SHOWER VALVE / SHOWER HEAD, both DELTA). The WC model on the page is C454CUFG#01; both sets emit two truncated variants of it, which is both a misread and a duplicate.
